reviews.author: SeekJohn14v6
reviews.text:
I parked by the Lakehouse tap and checked out the beautiful lake, which seems to be packed with fish.

Then I travelled to the trails that I took a picture of. The forest trails are nice and well kept. Plenty of flora and fauna all around. There is also a trail to a quarry pond which is pretty cool.

The lush forest provided excellent cooling shade as I explored the area. The forest loop trail had a very interesting tree that had a hole in it, check it out on my pics.

The lake area had plenty of benches with grills and there was even a boat rental place and a store for goods. Nice bathrooms and accomodations. A very nice park to visit with your friends and family. Enjoy!

reviews.author: Deborah W.
reviews.text: Beautiful Fellowship with my Camping Buddies, Family, and Friends!  They played volleyball, rode their bikes and roller skating, went swimming 🏊‍♂️, and adults and youth raising.  Other campers, kids, and Family joined us in fun activities to including dining with us.  This was a beautiful day.  Thank you to park Staff Gentleman for putting up the Volleyball net because my extended family had a Volleyball ready!  We had three sites together ❤️

reviews.author: Logan M.
reviews.text: This campground is awesome. Spots are large, open, and plenty of flat ground for a tent or three. Definitely recommend walking to the lake but the real highlight was the old growth forest trails! Budget out at least an hour or two to walk around the trails but maybe take some extra time! The campground itself can be quite loud on weekends in the summer but the trails were super quiet and peaceful. A little something for everyone. Would definitely go again!

reviews.author: J W.
reviews.text:
The lake and trails are great with super friendly staff!  We go every chance we get.  It can get pretty crowded around the water and swimming areas as well as the campsites are pretty full in good weather but it is worth it!

Just watch out for fishing line along the edges of the water.  My dog got caught in some line and I had to go in to untangle him.

reviews.author: Ben S.
reviews.text: Big chill! Great forest camping. The sites are spacious and clean. The other campers were respectful, some kids but not too loud. Most sites are in the trees and shaded. Lots of trails to walk or run. Bathrooms are nice with toilet paper and shower facility.

reviews.author: gdeakins
reviews.title: Rv camping
reviews.text: Popular for camping families with lots of trails to explore, swimming and fishing. Deep lake is well stocked with fish and there are paddle boats and boards available to rent. The lake is a little small and does not offer much in the way of exploring opportunities by kayak or canoe. Campsites are plentiful and sited very close to one another offering little privacy. There are cottages and glamping tents available if so inclined. I prefer camp sites with more privacy and access to larger bodies of water for kayaking. Great for day use, average for camping.

reviews.author: luv2trip2
reviews.title: Rv camping
reviews.text:
Millersylvania has all the charm of a better state park in WA. Around 80 acres with lots of things to explore. The park is on Deep Lake with excellent access from the park for swimming, fishing, etc. There are only a few houses on the lake so it feels like you are pretty remote. The lake is a 5 to 7 minute walk from about any camp site. There are boat rentals (canoe, kayak, pedal boat, paddle board), concessions, picnic areas (covered and uncovered). There is a very nice beer and wine garden with some warm food available. Some of the buildings were constructed in the 30s during the civil works administration and are very cool. The restrooms were ok and minimally maintained. There are pay showers. We stayed in the modern version of the Pampered Wilderness "cabins". That was a fun experience, but for what you have to pay per night the luxury cabins "tents" should have had their own bathroom and showers. We were bummed that there were no programs or movies at the amphitheater at night. Nearby is the town of Tenino with has a wince tasting, a candy shop and some small stores. There is a public swimming area right in town that is part of an old sand stone quarry; $4 per person, very unique and refreshing on a hot day.

Wolf Haven is also just a few minutes away as is Great Wolf Lodge Water Park.

We had breakfast at Farm Boy's and Country Cousins. Overall a very fun weekend.

reviews.author: Don H
reviews.text:
I am a long time resident of Washington and have visited almost all of the state parks.. This one is very nice and located in Olympia's backyard so to speak...

But $30 for a small camp space without electricity it's just too much... Add to this the fact that you get to spend more to take a shower too... Oh yes and the $30 discover pass, for day use parking...

Why is this? The legislature in their wisdom have severely cut state park budgets... Really cut... And I see lots of facilities deterating over time even at this time of high user fees..

I do NOT blame park employees, but our legislators that still do not have a budget with a week to go before state wide shutdowns...

Tell them about this nice state park gem!

reviews.author: David R
reviews.text: One of the more overlooked areas. A great place to go kayaking, hiking and potentially biking. Although preferably no biking please.

reviews.author: Jerrod K
reviews.text: The park offers many campsites which is great for groups book side by side. Some challenges I've experienced are many sites are small and don't support a flat area for a larger tent. We are a family of five, so i like privacy when i can get it. This is a great option for those that may not have booked reservations well in advance of peak camping dates.

reviews.author: JulieI339
reviews.title: Thick Forests
reviews.text: I timed my visit to this park perfectly! The weather was mild and sunny, but there was hardly anyone around. The bathrooms were pristine and had soap. The lake was clear, and even had a few kids playing in it, despite it only being April 2! The trails were mostly flat and pretty smooth, as forest trails go. The trees are gorgeous--many huge Douglas firs, mossy cedars, some alders and others.

reviews.author: Deborah C
reviews.text: there is overnight camping, day camping, and picnicking available here. Set on the Shore of a smaller lake, that people like to fish, swim and enjoy. Set in a heavily wooded area, perfect for hot summer days.

reviews.author: kellybE4148XX
reviews.text: After living here for 15 years, we finally check out MSP. The lake is long and shallow, so warms up nicely in the summer, and with a sandy beach, it's perfect for the younger kids. No boats allowed, but is perfect for paddle boarding, or kayaking. The trails around the parks are well marked. There are large log cabin pavilions that are available to rent for parties or other occasions. It's very quiet. You really feel that you are out in the woods.

reviews.author: randym21
reviews.text: The park has a bunch of different hiking trails that are easy. In the fall you will see some nice colors. There is some old growth trees as well. This is an ideal hike for your dog on a leash. Can be very crowded on weekends. Only a few miles from Olympia and very accessible.

reviews.author: 409rexm
reviews.text: Great place to walk through the woods or boat/fish on the lake. It is sort of an unknown gem that we discovered and would recommend for a day trip or outing to anyone.

reviews.author: iris0507
reviews.title: State Park with Many Amenities!
reviews.text: Millersylvania State Park offers a number of options for both day visitors and overnight campers. The park has an vintage state park feel with roomy campsites and old-style picnic tables. Swimming area is sandy and welcoming with free life jackets. Hiking trails abound! Close to nearby Olympia, Tacoma, and Seattle, this park is popular with locals and out of towners alike!

reviews.author: 505allenl
reviews.title: Great local hike area
reviews.text: This state park is close to downtown Olympia and has some great hiking and caping sites. The level is not too stressful and we even had elderly people who managed easily;y.

reviews.author: bradleyb311
reviews.title: Millersylvania
reviews.text: Enjoyed a wonderful afternoon walking the trails. The best part was having a glass of wine in the charming beer garden in the middle of the park.

reviews.author: amr_ve
reviews.title: Beautiful and family-friendly
reviews.text: The park is beautiful and set out of the way enough to feel isolated even though it's really close to Olympia and I5. There were plenty of picnic spots overlooking the lake, and the scenery was nice. The trails were well-maintained and had plenty of space for multiple people or kids on bikes to pass each other. We had our infant with us, and most people had dogs or kids with them as well, but despite that it wasn't too loud.

reviews.author: chowieruns
reviews.title: Beautiful place to take a walk, picnic, spend an hour or the day
reviews.text: I was looking for a place to get to the water and this is it-trails along the lakeside, picnic tables right there, a dock with seats to look at the view, fish; roped off swimming areas (no lifeguard). Clean restroom for day visitors. There is overnight camping which I did not investigate.

reviews.author: 207traceyk
reviews.title: Loved the Lakeside Cabin rental
reviews.text: This was a girlfriend getaway, and the cottage rental was fantastic. Clean as a button, plenty of space and privacy, even tho it is located next to boat launch. This rental,would be suitable for a family, too, as there is a loft with 3 beds, plus a separate bedroom on first floor. We really enjoyed the lake views. Hiked the trails too. Even tho this was shoulder/off season, plenty to do, and in summer, there’s swimming, bike and boat rentals. What a great getaway.

reviews.author: meinoly
reviews.title: Great hiking trails.
reviews.text: In most respects, Millersylvania is a pretty typical state park. You can get a campsite for about the same price as a budget hotel room, there's a lake that is a good place for swimming on a hot summer day or a paddle at most any time, there are picnic tables. However, Millersylvania is extremely unusual in having one of the only remaining old-growth Douglas-fir forests in the Puget Lowland. The best parts of it are readily accessible by trail, located northwest of the lake, less than a mile from the lakeside parking area. All in all there are about 3 miles of pleasant forest hiking trails in the park. It's accessible year-round, but it's best to wear muck boots in the winter as some stretches of trail may be several inches deep in water. Birding is reasonably good, as is botanizing. I believe the lake is stocked with fish.

reviews.author: Michael F
reviews.text: Super clean and nice state park. Love the trails and the lake. Has a cool faerie trail system that feels magical. A great local close to city camping location without feeling close to a city.

reviews.author: Terri B
reviews.text: If you want to enjoy hiking in the great Pacific Northwest but don't have the stamina - this is a beautiful, simple place that's an easy walk. Go off season - Summer can be crowded.

reviews.author: Tom I
reviews.text: This is great for swimming, Kayaking, canoeing or just having a picnic. It is vary close to the freeway but you will feel you are way out away from everything.

reviews.author: maxona
reviews.text: I was given this as a good place to go for a walk. Glad I tried here. I used my GPS to find it, but there were a few small signs pointing to the Park the closer you get there. My biggest complaint is I felt that the maps were not great to help me find the initial trails from the parking area. Once I was on the walk, you occasionally come up to a map to tell you were you are. But finding the beginning to the trail was confusing for someone who had never been there before. I went there shortly after the rainy season began dying down. That being said, the first part of the walk was very wet. Annoyingly so. But once out of that, the walk was beautiful. Tall, large trees and plenty of lichen and moss to feel you are visiting the Rain Forest. If you like to hike, and do not want too challenging of a hike, this is a good one. Not totally flat, but no climbing involved. Once on the trails, they are pretty easily marked and it is not too long of a hike either. They have picnic tables and barbecues for picnics, as well as camping sites.
